title: Latency-Adaptive Phase Sharding with Kernel-Cost Feedback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: In mixed workloads our current phase-splitting heuristics are either too aggressive (increasing overhead and hurting throughput) or too conservative (causing p95/p99 latency spikes for low-latency requests). We lack a tight feedback loop from kernel-level cost signals (measured FLOPs, attention memory hotspots, quantization path selection) back into the scheduler, so the allocator cannot make fine-grained sharding decisions that balance latency and throughput at the token-phase level.

Goal: Introduce a scheduler policy that shards large prefill/decode phases into adaptive micro-shards using real-time kernel-cost feedback. The policy should: (1) reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive requests without materially lowering sustained throughput, (2) avoid pathological fragmentation overhead, and (3) be safe to roll out per-customer and per-route with canarying and automatic rollback thresholds.
proposed_solution:
1) Instrument runtime kernels to emit lightweight cost hints per phase: an aggregated kernel_cost_score that encodes estimated compute intensity and memory pressure (string token). This will be an additive, low-cardinality signal to avoid telemetry bloat.

2) Implement a Phase Sharder stage in the existing prefill/decode pipeline that: a) consumes kernel_cost_score + request latency SLO tag + recent queueing headroom; b) decides between: no-shard, conservative micro-shard (2-4 sub-phases), or aggressive micro-shard (5-12 sub-phases). The sharder uses an exponential backoff for micro-shard sizing to bound extra scheduling overhead.

3) Kernel-aware hedging: for shards where kernel_cost_score is high and p95 latency risk exists, spawn lightweight hedged micro-slices (soft replica) prioritized on a separate low-latency pool. Hedged copies will use the same KV-cache pointers and cancel on first-token-return.

4) Feedback loop: after each request complete, collect actual observe_token_latency and kernel execution time, and feed a decayed moving-average back into the sharder policy to adjust thresholds per model and route.

5) Launch plan: feature-flagged rollout with two modes: observation-only (records decisions and outcomes) followed by canary (5% traffic) then ramp. Include per-route caps and a global overhead budget to prevent runaway fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: No >5% regression in sustained tokens/sec on benchmark throughput suite (bert-like and long-context chat workloads)
p95 latency improvement >= 12% on latency-tagged flows in synthetic tail-heavy tests compared to baseline scheduler
Overhead (extra scheduling ops and small kernel invocations) is < 3% of total CPU time under normal load
Safeguard: automatic rollback triggers if any route sees >10% token-cost increase or customer-visible error rate rise
rollout_plan: Phase A: observation-only for 2 weeks on shadowed traffic (metric collection only). Phase B: canary at 5% of traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99 and token cost; hold for 72 hours. Phase C: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% with per-route constraints. Finalize by promoting defaults for latency-tagged routes in runtime-1.20. Provide an escape hatch flag to disable hedging globally.

2025-02-18: Design review with infra: agreed to keep telemetry low-cardinality and emit only per-phase aggregated scores; added explicit global overhead budget. Action: Marco to open PR for kernel hint telemetry.
2025-02-22: Benchmarks run on p4d snapshot: conservative sharding decreased p99 by ~18% for short-chat tail but reduced global throughput by ~1.8% (within target).
